why: States the SPY same-day iron condor sold at 10:00 ET with 15-delta short strikes and 5-wide wings, one condor, closed at 15:30 ET or earlier once its price is up 150% on the credit (2.5 times it); the period is simply left unrestricted, which is the whole stored history the author meant.

Keeps the profit factor of the current iron condor backtest as the subject but folds the two requests into a single question, so it no longer clearly asks both for an explanation of the term and for its value.

Keeps IWM and the open more than 1% above the previous close, but asks how often the day closes below its open, which is a different event from the price trading back to the previous close at some point in the session and is not one of the accepted alternatives.
Changes only the streak to five consecutive up days and leaves SPY, the next-day outcome and the whole history as they were, which is the author's intent.

Keeps SPY and the close-above-the-previous-close outcome but turns the weak open into a gap down of any size, where the author meant a fall of at least 0.3% from the open over the first 15 minutes and explicitly not the gap.
Keeps one QQQ at-the-money put bought at 12:15 and sold at 12:55 every day in 2025, but drops the same-day expiration and leaves the zone as 'local time' instead of Pacific (15:15 to 15:55 New York).
Keeps the switch from the straddle to a strangle with everything else unchanged, but does not say how far out of the money the two legs are, which the author meant as about 1% each.
